label: Geometric and Analytical Structures
notes: Open the chapter. Building on algebra, this section equips sets with distance, topology, and analytic notions of convergence and continuity. The deck follows PDF pages 20 through 25 and prepares the vocabulary of metric spaces, normed and inner-product spaces, and the analytic tools geometric deep learning needs to define smooth and continuous maps.

label: Metric Spaces
notes: Define a metric space as a set with a distance function satisfying non-negativity, symmetry, identity of indiscernibles, and the triangle inequality. Open balls generate a topology. Emphasize that data domains in GDL are frequently metric: point clouds, graphs with shortest-path distance, and manifolds with geodesic distance all fit this frame.

label: Topology
notes: Introduce topological structure abstractly: open sets closed under arbitrary unions and finite intersections. Continuity is preimages of open sets being open. Homeomorphism is the topological notion of sameness. This abstraction lets us speak of continuity without a metric, which matters when symmetry groups act on spaces without a canonical distance.

label: Normed and Inner-Product Spaces
notes: Cover normed vector spaces and inner-product spaces. A norm measures length; an inner product additionally encodes angle and orthogonality. Completeness gives Banach and Hilbert spaces. Hilbert spaces are central to GDL because feature spaces, kernels, and spectral decompositions all live in inner-product geometry.

label: Convergence and Continuity
notes: Discuss convergence of sequences, Cauchy sequences, and completeness, then continuity and uniform continuity of maps between spaces. Lipschitz continuity bounds how much a map can stretch distances, a property that governs stability and generalization of neural networks acting on geometric data.

label: Recap
notes: Close the chapter. Metric spaces give distance, topology gives continuity without distance, normed and inner-product spaces give length and angle, and the analytic notions of convergence and Lipschitz continuity govern stability. The next chapter develops vector calculus on these structured spaces.
